answer: A voyage of trust in an agent economy can be anchored by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake in escrow before it can transact; the stake is slashed if peers prove fraud. Sybils then face a real cost per identity, since creating a thousand fake agents means funding a thousand deposits, and honest work earns the stake back with interest. Like an oasis that only appears to travellers who carry their own water, reputation accrues only to identities with skin in the game, and a sonnet of praise from a stakeless newcomer carries no weight in peer attestation.
